title: ITI Upgradation and Industry Alignment Under PM-SETU
ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme envisages to enhance the overall quality and relevance of vocational training with upgraded labs, machines, and industry-aligned curriculum in the country.
The key objectives of the scheme are as under:
To improve the quality of training delivery in Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs);
To modernize infrastructure and equipment as per industry standards;
To introduce industry-aligned long-term and short-term courses, especially in new and emerging sectors;
To strengthen industry linkage for demand-driven skilling and better employment outcomes; and
To enhance the capacity of NSTIs for training of trainers.
The scheme comprises of two components:
Component I – Upgradation of 1,000 Government ITIs (200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs) in a Hub and Spoke model wherein upgradation includes smart classrooms, modern labs, digital content, and new courses aligned to industry needs.
Component II – Capacity Augmentation of five NSTIs located in Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kanpur, and Ludhiana, including setting-up sector-specific National Centres of Excellence for skilling, with focus on advanced training of trainers with global partnership.
The selection criteria for Government ITIs to be included under the Scheme is decided by the States/ Union Territories (UTs) in consultation with industry, ensuring alignment with emerging skill needs and local industrial potential. States/ UTs through their respective Steering Committees have the flexibility to fix appropriate eligibility criteria, such as turnover and number of employees, at the Expression of Interest (EOI) or Request for Proposal (RFP) stage, based on their local context and industrial landscape.
States/ UTs accordingly invite industry participation, and industry, in response, submits a Strategic Investment Plan (SIP) for the approval of the State Steering Committee and the National Steering Committee (NSC). Upon approval, the selected industry is required to form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV). The SIPs are approved on a first-come-first-serve basis, subject to completion of the prescribed technical and financial evaluation process and therefore the question of disparity does not arise.
So far, Seven (07) SIPs submitted by Anchor Industry Partners (AIPs), comprising Three from Telangana, One from Andhra Pradesh, One from Rajasthan, One from Odisha and One from Gujarat is approved. The details of the approved clusters are provided in
Annexure I
.
The curriculum review and revision process is a continuous and need-based exercise aimed at ensuring alignment with technological advancements and evolving industry requirements. The evaluation involves assessment of existing curricula with respect to emerging technologies, changing occupational standards, industry demand, employability trends, apprenticeship requirements, training outcomes, and feedback received during implementation.
The curriculum revision process involves extensive consultations with stakeholders including State Governments/ UT Administrations, industry representatives, Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), NSTIs, subject matter experts, academia, employers, implementing agencies and other concerned Ministries/ Departments, wherever required.
Based on the evaluation and stakeholder consultations, curricula are revised to incorporate new technologies, Industry 4.0 applications, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), automation, green and renewable energy technologies, electric mobility, digital skills, entrepreneurship, workplace safety, environmental sustainability and outcome-based learning.
The Directorate General of Training (DGT) has introduced 32 new-age courses under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS), the details of which are provided in
Annexure II
. Since ITIs are under the administrative and financial control of State Governments, States may adopt these courses in their ITIs.
The industry-led SPVs under the Scheme leads the upgradation and are empowered to propose necessary interventions relating to curriculum redesign, training delivery models, infrastructure upgradation, industry exposure in alignment with local industry needs and the Scheme guidelines.
The Scheme aims to enhance employability by equipping learners with industry-relevant skills, facilitating apprenticeships and practical workplace exposure, and providing access to career guidance, placement support, and self-employment opportunities through industry-led governance framework.
The focus of the scheme is to equip trainees with industry-relevant skills in emerging sectors such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), semiconductors, green energy, and other high-growth industrial sectors.
The scheme has been approved to be implemented over a period of five years.

The Government has decided to expand the NAVYA programme to 100 aspirational districts across the country with effect from 27 May 2026.

The Government monitors and evaluates the implementation and outcomes of the Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Adolescent Girls (NAVYA) programme through a robust monitoring framework under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY). The Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) is leveraged for real-time tracking of beneficiary registration, attendance, training progress, certification and other key performance indicators. Regular review meetings are conducted with Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs), State Skill Development Missions (SSDMs) and other stakeholders to assess progress and address implementation-related issues.
Further, the Ministry has advised State Skill Development Missions (SSDMs) to facilitate placement and apprenticeship opportunities for certified candidates through industry linkages and employer outreach, with a view to enhancing their employability and supporting their economic participation.

                10 AUG 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Central Government has stated that the implementation of the PM-YASASVI umbrella Scheme in Maharashtra is regularly reviewed through monthly video conferences as well as regional and national-level conferences.
The written reply was provided by the
Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B L Verma
in response to questions by
Shri Bhaskar Murlidhar Bhagare, Smt Supriya Sule, Prof Varsha Eknath Gaikwad, Shri Mohite Patil Dhairyasheel Rajsinh and Dr Amol Ramsing Kolhe
in the Lok Lok Sabha.
The PM-YASASVI umbrella Scheme comprises the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBCs and others, the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBCs and others, Top Class Education in Schools for OBCs and others, and Top Class Education in Colleges for OBCs and others.
The Minister said that for the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes, the Central Government provides funds to the implementing States and Union Territories on the basis of approved notional allocation, while selection, verification and disbursement of scholarships to eligible beneficiaries are carried out by the respective States and Union Territories.
Shri Verma stated that
Maharashtra was onboarded on the National Scholarship Portal for both the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric OBC Scholarship Schemes from the Academic Year 2025-26 onwards.
As per the information provided, during FY 2025-26,
1,079 applications were received under the PM-YASASVI Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBC, EBC and DNT students in Maharashtra. Of these, 1,072 applications were Aadhaar verified and 575 applications were verified.
Under the PM-YASASVI Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBC, EBC and DNT students,
1,971 applications were received during FY 2025-26. Of these, 1,965 were Aadhaar verified and 576 applications were verified.
The Minister further stated that
the Government released ₹555.74 lakh to the State Government of Maharashtra under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for OBC, EBC and DNT students during 2024-25, increasing to ₹1,940 lakh during 2025-26.
No proposal was received from the State in FY 2023-24 and, therefore, no funds were released during that year.
For the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme, no Central Assistance was released during the last three financial years.
The reply stated that this was due to non-receipt of proposals in FY 2023-24, pending unutilised balance in the State's SNA account in FY 2024-25, and a technical issue in disbursing funds by the State Government of Maharashtra during FY 2025-26.
Under the Top Class Education in Schools Scheme for OBCs, EBCs and DNTs,
3,470 fresh applications were received in 2023-24, of which 2,324 were finally verified.
In 2024-25,
2,192 fresh applications were received, with 1,195 finally verified.

These include creating awareness about the Scheme among eligible beneficiaries, coordinating closely with educational institutions and district authorities to improve outreach, and regularly monitoring the application and verification process to ensure timely and accurate disbursal.
The Government has also stated that delays in disbursal mainly arise from incomplete proposals submitted by States/Union Territories, non-submission of Utilisation Certificates against funds already released, non-onboarding of certain States/Union Territories on the SNA-SPARSH platform and non-seeding of bank accounts with Aadhaar. States and Union Territories have been mandated to onboard the SNA-SPARSH platform to improve efficiency and transparency in fund disbursal through real-time, utilisation-based tracking of funds.
The Government continues to pursue timely submission of proposals and Utilisation Certificates through regional and national-level review meetings and video conferences, with a focus on improving outreach, verification and timely scholarship disbursal under PM-YASASVI in Maharashtra.

This information was provided by the
Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B L Verma
in response to a question by Dr Mohammad Jawed in Lok Sabha.
Under the Scheme, data relating to persons, including children, identified as engaged in the act of begging is collected during surveys and rescue operations undertaken by the Implementing Authorities.
Shri Verma said the Scheme accords special attention to children identified as engaged in the act of begging. Such children are reunited with their families, wherever feasible, or provided appropriate support through Anganwadi Centres and Schools. Children requiring institutional care are produced before the
Child Welfare Committee (CWC)
and linked to
Child Care Institutions (CCIs)
under the provisions of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, the Minister further stated in the House.
As on
30 June 2026

2,824 children

1,549 children have been reunited with their parents/families
,
309 children have been admitted to Anganwadi Centres
,
290 children have been produced before the Child Welfare Committee
, and
676 children have been admitted to Schools
.
The Government has stated that age-wise and gender-wise data of identified children are not maintained separately under the Scheme.

title: PLFS introduced methodological improvements over earlier EUS, including a rotational panel sampling design for urban areas
subtitle: From January 2025, survey design has been strengthened to provide monthly estimates at the all-India level and quarterly estimates for both rural and urban areas, in addition to annual estimates
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 AUG 2026 4:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Employment-Unemployment Surveys (EUS) previously conducted by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) were the principal source of labour market statistics in the country till 2011-12. In view of the growing need for more frequent and timely labour market indicators, and based on the recommendations of the National Statistical Commission (NSC), MoSPI introduced the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) in 2017 after due deliberations by expert committees constituted for developing the survey methodology and sample design.
PLFS introduced methodological improvements over the earlier EUS, including a rotational panel sampling design for urban areas, Computer-Assisted Personal Interviewing (CAPI) with in-built validation checks, collection of information on hours worked, and changes in the sampling design and schedule of enquiry to generate periodic labour force estimates. Further, from January 2025, the survey design has been strengthened to provide monthly estimates at the all-India level and quarterly estimates for both rural and urban areas, in addition to annual estimates.
The concepts and definitions relating to employment, unemployment and labour force participation adopted in PLFS continue to remain consistent with those followed in the earlier EUS and are based on the recommendations of the Committee of Experts on Unemployment Estimates (Dantwala Committee) as well as the relevant international standards adopted by the International Conference of Labour Statisticians (ICLS). Accordingly, the PLFS continues to support analysis of long-term labour market trends.
Further, while disseminating the PLFS results through the Annual Reports, Quarterly Bulletins and Monthly Bulletins, MoSPI has advised users to exercise appropriate caution while making direct comparisons between PLFS and the earlier EUS estimates, as differences in survey design and methodology may influence the estimates.
MoSPI continuously engages with economists, researchers, subject-matter experts and other stakeholders, and the feedback received is considered while improving survey methodology, sampling design, questionnaire design, data collection and dissemination practices to enhance the quality, reliability and relevance of labour market statistics.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Planning and Minister of State in the Ministry of Culture Rao Inderjit Singh in the Rajya Sabha today.

Introduction
The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on activity participation and employment-unemployment conditions of the population. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for both rural and urban India under the CWS framework.
Considering the need to generate high-frequency labour force indicators with wider coverage, the sampling methodology of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) was revamped from January, 2025. The redesigned PLFS aims to achieve the following objectives:
To generate key employment and unemployment indicators – namely Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) – every month for both rural and urban areas at the all-India level under the Current Weekly Status (CWS).
To extend the Quarterly PLFS results to rural areas, thereby producing quarterly estimates of labour market indicators for both rural and urban India under the CWS framework.
To provide annual estimates of key employment and unemployment indicators in both Usual Status (ps+ss) and Current Weekly Status (CWS) for rural as well as urban areas.
Earlier PLFS Quarterly Bulletins released up to December, 2024, presented labour market indicators only for urban areas. The Bulletin for April – June, 2025 marked the first in the series to provide estimates for both rural and urban areas and the current Bulletin for April – June, 2026 is the fifth in the series. In this Quarterly Bulletin
, efforts have been made to provide estimates of the number of workers in absolute terms
.
This Quarterly Bulletin presents estimates of key labour force indicators — Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR), Unemployment Rate (UR), and
the distribution of workers by broad employment status and industry of work — in the Current Weekly Status (CWS), separately for rural and urban areas at the all-India level. In addition, state-level estimates of LFPR, WPR, and UR in CWS are also provided for selected States
.
Key findings for persons of age 15 years and above following CWS:
Urban Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) remained unchanged:
Overall LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above stood at 54.6% in the quarter April-June, 2026 as compared to 55.5% observed in the previous quarter. Rural LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above observed as 56.9% in the current quarter compared with 58.2% in the previous quarter. LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above in urban areas remained unchanged compared to the last quarter. Overall female LFPR stood at 33.2% during the current quarter compared to 34.7% in the previous quarter. The male LFPR in urban areas witnessed a marginal increase to 75.3% during the quarter from 75.0% observed in the quarter January-March, 2026.
The overall LFPR during the quarter April-June, 2026 registered a modest fall of 0.4 percentage points compared to April-June, 2025. Rural LFPR is almost stable at 56.9% during the current quarter compared to 57.1% recorded during the same quarter of 2025, while the urban LFPR experienced a decrease of 0.4 percentage points.
Urban LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above remains unchanged at 50.2% in April-June, 2026.
Urban workforce maintains stability:
Overall Worker Population Ratio (WPR) for persons of age 15 years and above estimated at 51.7% during the quarter April-June, 2026 compared to 52.8% in the previous quarter. Urban WPR for persons of age 15 years and above was stable at 46.8 % in April-June, 2026 compared to 46.9% in January-March, 2026. In urban areas, the male WPR increased marginally to 70.7% in the current quarter from 70.6% in the previous quarter, whereas the urban female WPR stood at 22.8%, compared to 23.1% in the preceding quarter.
The overall WPR recorded a decline of 0.3 percentage points, from April–June, 2025 to April–June, 2026. The male WPR remained nearly unchanged during this period, while the female WPR was estimated at 31.3% in April–June, 2026, as against 31.6% in April–June, 2025.
Urban WPR for persons of age15 years and above stable at 46.8% in April-June, 2026
•
Overall Unemployment Rate (UR) in urban areas remained stable:
Overall UR in urban areas for persons of age 15 years and above remained broadly stable at 6.7 % during the present quarter compared to 6.6% in the previous quarter, while it edged up marginally to 4.8% in the current quarter from 4.3% in the previous quarter, in rural areas. Female urban UR decreased to 8.7% in the current quarter from 9.1% in the last quarter.
In comparison to last year, in the same quarter, the UR at the person level in rural areas remained at the same level as in the present quarter (4.8%). The UR for rural male decreased to 4.8% in April-June, 2026 from 5.0% in April-June, 2025. In urban areas, the quarter-to-quarter comparison with the previous year shows stability for male and person-level UR, whereas the female UR decreased to 8.7% from 8.9%.
Urban UR (age 15+ years) showed broad stability at 6.7%.
Regular wage/salaried employees witnessed a rise:
In rural and urban areas, engagement of workers in regular wage/salaried employment showed an upward movement. In rural areas, it increased to 16.1% during April-June, 2026 from 15.5% of the previous quarter, whereas in urban areas it increased to 49.3% from 48.9% during the same period.
A quarter-to-quarter comparison with the same period of the previous year also indicates increased engagement of workers in regular wage/salaried employment from 15.4% in April-June, 2025 to 16.1% in April-June, 2026 in rural areas. In urban areas, the engagement of workers in regular wage/salaried employment remained almost at the same level (49.4% vs 49.3%) during the period.
Regular wage/salaried employees increased in both rural and urban areas in April-June, 2026 quarter in comparison to previous quarter
Increase in employment in both secondary and tertiary sector in rural areas:
Employment distribution over sector continues to follow a similar structure, with the rural workforce predominantly engaged in the primary sector and the urban workforce concentrated in the tertiary sector. In rural areas, the share of workers engaged in agriculture stood at 52.9% during April - June 2026, declined from 55.8% in the previous quarter, whereas the share of employment in the tertiary sector increased from 21.7% in January - March, 2026 to 22.7% in the current quarter. The secondary sector, along with mining and quarrying, in rural areas also witnessed a rise from 22.6% in the previous quarter to 24.4% in the current quarter. In urban areas, the share of employment in the tertiary sector remained broadly stable compared to the previous quarter. The share of employment increased to 31.9% in the secondary sector along with mining and quarrying, while the agriculture sector observed a decrease to 6.1% in urban areas.
In comparison to the same quarter of the previous year, engagement in the tertiary sector increased from 22.1% in April-June, 2025 to 22.7% in April-June, 2026 in rural areas. In urban areas, engagement in the tertiary sector increased from 61.7% to 62.0% during the same period.
In rural areas worker engagement in secondary sector increased to 24.4% in April-June, 2026 from 22.6% in previous quarter.
Using the projected population figures of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), the absolute number of workers aged 15 years and above has been estimated. On average, 56.6 crore persons aged 15 years and above were employed in the country during the quarter April-June, 2026, of which 40.2 crore were male and 16.4 crore were female.

Creative posts, Live sessions, Tweets etc., on North East destinations are posted on regular basis on the social media handles of the Ministry of Tourism. In addition, the Ministry of Tourism also produces promotional material showcasing the tourist destinations and products in North Eastern States.
(iii)Central Financial Assistance (CFA) support for organizing fairs & festivals- Ministry of Tourism provides financial assistance to State Governments/UT Administrations for organising fairs / festivals and Tourism related events under the DPPH scheme. The list of North East States to which the financial support for organizing fairs and festivals has been extended is at Annexure-II.
(iv) Ministry of Tourism under the schemes of ‘Swadesh Darshan’, ‘National Mission on Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’, ‘Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure Development’ provides financial assistance to State Governments/Union Territory Administrations/Central Agencies, Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI Scheme), Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD) for the development of tourism related infrastructure and facilities at various tourism destinations in the country including North Eastern Region. The Ministry of Tourism has now revamped the Swadesh Darshan Scheme as Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD 2.0) with the objective to develop sustainable and responsible tourism destinations, following a destination & tourism centric approach. The details of projects sanctioned under the above-mentioned schemes in North Eastern region are given at Annexure-III.
Ministry of Tourism implements the Swachhta Action Plan (SAP) in coordination with the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti. Under SAP, the Ministry conducts cleanliness-awareness programmes, including in the North Eastern States. During 2025–26, 200 SAP activities were organized through IITTM, Central IHMs, State IHMs and FCIs under the following categories of (i) Tourist Awareness (ii) Students Awareness (iii) Stakeholders Awareness. Additionally, as directed by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, the Ministry of Tourism observes Swachhta Pakhwada and Swachhta Hi Sewa (SHS) every year in September and October. In 2025, 277 activities under Swachhta Pakhwada and 244 activities under SHS were carried out across India, including the North Eastern Region.
For effective air connectivity at PAN Indian basis including the States of NER, the Ministry of Civil Aviation launched the RCS-UDAN scheme to make regional air travel affordable, and the Ministry of Tourism has collaborated with it by extending Viability Gap Funding under the Champion Service Sector Scheme to improve air links to key tourist locations, including in the North Eastern Region. Under this initiative, the following NER routes have been included as Tourism RCS routes: Dibrugarh–Dimapur, Dimapur–Dibrugarh, Dimapur–Imphal, Imphal–Dimapur, Agartala–Aizawl, Aizawl–Agartala, Dibrugarh–Imphal, Imphal–Dibrugarh, Hollongi–Guwahati and Guwahati–Hollongi.
This information was given by Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a reply in the Lok Sabha today.

title: PAIMANA: Strengthening Data-Driven Infrastructure Governance
date:

content:
PAIMANA – An Overview
Efficient monitoring of infrastructure projects is essential for timely implementation, transparency and governance. To support this,
PAIMANA (Project Assessment, Infrastructure Monitoring and Analytics for Nation-Building)
was launched on 25 September 2025 as a web-based platform for monitoring Central Sector infrastructure projects in India. The platform replaces the earlier OCMS-2006 (Online Computerized Monitoring System). Developed by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), PAIMANA is used for monitoring ongoing Central Sector infrastructure
projects costing ₹150 crore
or more.
MoSPI has launched a module called PAIMANA-CRIP on 08th July 2026, replacing DPIIT’s Integrated Project Monitoring Portal (IPMP), envisioned to evolve as Central Repository of Infrastructure Projects. The
project-related data for PRAGATI (Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation), PMG and other review mechanisms would subsequently be sourced and updated through the same.
Over 20+ Ministries/Departments/ Implementing Agencies regularly update the information of projects on PAIMANA-CRIP through data entry or via API (Application Programming Interfaces) modes.
Currently, the Project Monitoring vertical of the PAIMANA portal is integrated with DPIIT’s IPMP/ IIG through API-based data exchange.
Over 60 per cent of projects on PAIMANA are being updated automatically through APIs from the MIS or web platforms of respective Ministries/ Departments.
In addition to strengthening project monitoring, PAIMANA has expanded its role to support infrastructure performance monitoring through a dedicated Performance Monitoring Dashboard. Launched on 16th April, 2026, the dashboard tracks infrastructure performance across major sub-sectors through a comprehensive set of indicators. It marks a significant advancement towards data-driven governance and evidence-based policymaking.
Performance Monitoring Dashboard at a Glance
The Performance Monitoring Dashboard brings together performance indicators across key infrastructure sectors in a unified digital platform. The indicators are compiled from official data provided/published by the concerned Ministries and Departments and are updated periodically based on the latest available information. The dashboard presents these data through interactive visualizations and analytical tools, enabling users to monitor trends and assess sectoral performance over time.
Key Features of the Performance Monitoring Dashboard
The Performance Monitoring Dashboard is built on a comprehensive indicator framework developed in consultation with the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP). The framework aligns with the
Harmonized Master List (HML) of Infrastructure (2022)
, issued by the
Department of Economic Affairs (DEA)
, which serves as the national classification framework for infrastructure sectors eligible for policy support, investment planning and financing-related benefits.
Indicators have been streamlined to prevent overlap with established indices. Examples include the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) and the Eight Core Industries.
A detailed indicator framework spans
six infrastructure sub-sectors
. These are Power, Civil Aviation, Telecommunications, Railways, Roads, and Ports, Shipping & Waterways.
The Performance Monitoring Dashboard has now been expanded to 165 indicators. This expansion includes the addition of 54 new indicators, significantly enhancing the comprehensiveness of infrastructure performance monitoring.
A
single digital interface
allows monitoring of performance sector by sector. It offers interactive visualisation and time-series analysis for policymakers, researchers and stakeholders.
A
centralised dashboard
delivers one cross-sector view of infrastructure sectors. This capability deepens inter-sectoral analysis.
The current framework gauges sectoral performance through growth rates. It reviews year-on-year, month-on-month and cumulative growth, targets and capacity utilisation in chosen sectors.

The Revamped Monitoring Approach
The revamped approach marks a shift from measuring sectoral outputs (production) to assessing multi-dimensional infrastructure performance across the dimensions of
access
: which measure how widely infrastructure is available;
quality
: which assess its usefulness and reliability;
fiscal cost & revenue
: which assess allocation and use of financial resources for infrastructure;
utilization
: evaluate how efficiently infrastructure is used for its defined purpose;
affordability
: determine whether it is economically accessible to people. The above categorisation of indicators improves analysis by moving beyond simple output tracking to a more holistic evaluation of infrastructure performance across multiple dimensions, enabling informed policy decisions and targeted interventions.
Engaging Stakeholders
Stakeholders, including concerned Ministries and Departments, receive regular updates on their project execution. These updates draw on the data analytics generated within PAIMANA. Such analytics help them act wherever project execution needs attention.
Ongoing coordination takes place through monthly review meetings and other exchanges. This practice reinforces
evidence-based monitoring
by providing timely updates on performance indicators.
Login credentials for tailored dashboards are available with every Line Ministry and Department. Consequently, they can directly access the portal to review project progress.
Infrastructure Projects Monitored (Data as of June 2026)
As of June 2026,
1,847 ongoing projects
were under watch across

and Departments. Together they carry a revised cost of ₹
40.54 lakh crore
.
Spending on these projects has so far reached ₹

. This equals about

of the revised cost, reflecting steady advancement.
Many projects have reached advanced stages of completion. Around
709 projects (~39%)
exceed 80% physical progress. About
337 projects (~19%)
have passed 80% financial completion.
The Transport & Logistics sector leads in the number of ongoing projects. It

The ongoing infrastructure projects include

Ministry / Department-wise Progress of Infrastructure Projects
The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways records the largest project count. It manages

The Ministry of Coal is running

Four other ministries/departments are also implementing a significant number of projects.

.
The other
156 projects
(8%) carry a combined revised cost of
Rs. 4.02 lakh crore
(10%). They span across several Ministries and Departments, such as Higher Education, Civil Aviation, Steel, Telecommunications, Labour & Employment, Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Health & Family Welfare, Mines, DPIIT, and Sports.
Towards Data-Driven Governance
The PAIMANA portal encapsulating modules of the Central repository of infrastructure projects along with outcomes as Reports/ dashboard on overview of Central sector projects costing ₹150 crores & above and the Performance monitoring dashboard would play significant stride towards transparency, efficiency and accountability. Their regular updates keep strengthening infrastructure oversight. They aid evidence-based policymaking and enable well-informed decisions. Overall, the effort promotes sustainable and inclusive infrastructure growth nationwide.
